blocks.title: Jamestown (1607)
blocks.desc: First permanent English settlement in North America, in Virginia.

blocks.title: Plymouth & the Mayflower Compact (1620)
blocks.desc: Pilgrims agree to govern themselves — an early example of self-government.

blocks.title: The Thirteen Colonies
blocks.desc: New England, Middle and Southern colonies, each shaped by geography and economy.

blocks.title: No taxation without representation
blocks.desc: Colonists protest taxes such as the Stamp Act (1765) passed without their vote.

blocks.title: Declaration of Independence (1776)
blocks.desc: Adopted July 4, 1776; written mainly by Thomas Jefferson.

blocks.title: Victory at Yorktown (1781)
blocks.desc: The British surrender at Yorktown ends major fighting.

blocks.title: Articles of Confederation
blocks.desc: First U.S. government; a weak central government without the power to tax.

blocks.title: Constitutional Convention (1787)
blocks.desc: Delegates in Philadelphia write the Constitution, signed September 17, 1787.

blocks.title: Bill of Rights (1791)
blocks.desc: The first ten amendments protect individual rights.

blocks.title: Causes of the Civil War
blocks.desc: Disagreements over slavery and states' rights divide North and South.

blocks.title: Emancipation Proclamation (1863)
blocks.desc: Lincoln declares enslaved people in Confederate states free.

blocks.title: Juneteenth (1865)
blocks.desc: June 19, 1865: freedom announced to enslaved people in Galveston, Texas.

blocks.title: 19th Amendment (1920)
blocks.desc: Women gain the right to vote.

blocks.title: Civil Rights Movement
blocks.desc: Brown v. Board (1954) and the Civil Rights Act (1964) fight segregation and discrimination.

blocks.title: Moon landing (1969)
blocks.desc: Apollo 11 astronauts walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

blocks.title: Legislative branch
blocks.desc: Congress (Senate and House of Representatives) makes laws.

blocks.title: Executive branch
blocks.desc: The President carries out and enforces laws.

blocks.title: Judicial branch
blocks.desc: The courts, led by the Supreme Court, interpret laws.

blocks.title: Checks and balances
blocks.desc: Each branch can limit the power of the others.

blocks.title: Federalism
blocks.desc: Power is shared between the national and state governments.

blocks.title: Popular sovereignty
blocks.desc: The government's power comes from the people.

blocks.title: Local government
blocks.desc: Cities and counties: mayors, city councils, school boards.

blocks.title: State government
blocks.desc: Texas: the Governor, the Legislature and state courts in Austin.

blocks.title: National government
blocks.desc: The federal government in Washington, D.C.

blocks.title: Cardinal & intermediate directions
blocks.desc: N, S, E, W and NE, NW, SE, SW on a compass rose.

blocks.title: Latitude & longitude
blocks.desc: Imaginary lines used to find absolute location.

blocks.title: Parts of a map
blocks.desc: Title, legend (key), scale and compass rose.

blocks.title: Coastal Plains
blocks.desc: Largest region; Houston, farmland and the Gulf coast.

blocks.title: North Central Plains
blocks.desc: Rolling hills and prairies; Dallas–Fort Worth area.

blocks.title: Great Plains
blocks.desc: High, flat land; the Panhandle and Edwards Plateau.

blocks.title: Mountains and Basins
blocks.desc: Driest region; El Paso and Big Bend.

blocks.title: Adapting to the environment
blocks.desc: People change how they live to fit climate and land.

blocks.title: Modifying the environment
blocks.desc: Dams, irrigation and roads change the land.

blocks.title: Natural resources
blocks.desc: Renewable and nonrenewable resources such as water, soil and oil.

blocks.title: Needs and wants
blocks.desc: Needs are required to live; wants are things people would like to have.

blocks.title: Goods and services
blocks.desc: Goods are things you can touch; services are work done for others.

blocks.title: Scarcity and choice
blocks.desc: Resources are limited, so people must make choices (opportunity cost).

blocks.title: Supply and demand
blocks.desc: Prices rise when demand is greater than supply.

blocks.title: Producers and consumers
blocks.desc: Producers make goods and services; consumers buy and use them.

blocks.title: Entrepreneurs
blocks.desc: People who start businesses and take risks.

blocks.title: Rights of citizens
blocks.desc: Freedoms such as speech, religion and voting.

blocks.title: Responsibilities of citizens
blocks.desc: Obeying laws, voting, serving on juries.

blocks.title: Voting and elections
blocks.desc: Citizens choose leaders through elections.

blocks.title: U.S. and Texas flags
blocks.desc: Flags, pledges and their meanings.

blocks.title: The Star-Spangled Banner
blocks.desc: The national anthem, written by Francis Scott Key in 1814.

blocks.title: National holidays
blocks.desc: Independence Day, Constitution Day, Veterans Day and more.

blocks.title: Customs and traditions
blocks.desc: Food, music, celebrations and language passed between generations.

blocks.title: Cultural diversity in Texas
blocks.desc: Native American, Mexican, African American, European and Asian heritage.

blocks.title: Contributions of groups
blocks.desc: How different groups have shaped Texas and the nation.

blocks.title: Inventions that changed life
blocks.desc: The telephone, the light bulb, the airplane and the computer.

blocks.title: Transportation and communication
blocks.desc: From horses and railroads to cars, planes and the internet.
